title: Grafana + CloudWatch -- building the pipeline dashboard
exp: With the workspace and IAM role in place, this is where you actually wire up CloudWatch as a data source and build the panels that show whether the 50-source pipeline is healthy.
pts: Adding the CloudWatch data source inside Grafana: select the default region and the auth method (the workspace's attached IAM role handles this automatically on AMG -- no access keys to paste in).
The CloudWatch metrics query editor has four required fields: namespace, metric name, dimensions (filters down to one specific resource), and statistic (Average, Maximum, Sum, etc.) over a period.

CloudWatch Logs as a Grafana query type: you can paste a Logs Insights query directly into a panel. With a `stats` aggregation producing numeric output, Grafana renders it as a time series; without one, it renders as a raw log list.
Metric Math lets you combine two queries into a third: query A = error count, query B = total count, query C = 100*(A/B) renders directly as an error-rate percentage panel.

Template variables sourced from a CloudWatch dimension value (e.g. a $source dropdown built from the Source dimension on your custom Pipeline/Orders metric) let one dashboard serve all 50 sources without 50 separate dashboards.

Practical panel set for the 50-source pipeline: records processed per source (Stat), job duration trend (Time series), error rate % (Stat, Metric Math), EMR IsIdle (Stat, cost signal), last successful run timestamp per source (Table).
pr: Build a Grafana panel using Metric Math that computes error rate as a percentage from two CloudWatch metrics

qa.q: What four things does a CloudWatch metrics query in Grafana require?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Namespace (which metric family, e.g. Pipeline/Orders), metric name (RecordsProcessed), dimensions (which specific resource -- e.g. Source=Bloomberg), and statistic over a period (Sum, Average, Maximum, etc. aggregated per time bucket). All four are required to fully specify which numbers to retrieve -- omitting dimensions returns an aggregate across all resources in that namespace, which is rarely what you want.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.

qa.q: How do you turn a CloudWatch Logs Insights query into a time-series panel instead of a raw log table?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Include a stats aggregation with a bin() time grouping in the query, e.g. stats avg(duration_ms) as avg_duration by bin(1h). Without an aggregation, Grafana renders the matched log lines as a scrolling list (the Logs panel view). With one, it produces numeric values per time bucket that Grafana can plot as a line or bar chart, exactly like a metrics query.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** EF Core builds an Expression Tree, translates it via the relational SQL provider into a parameterized T-SQL query, and materializes entities into the DbContext Change Tracker. N+1 queries occur when navigating un-included navigation properties in a loop.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Executing queries without AsNoTracking() in read-only APIs forces EF Core to keep snapshot copies of all returned entities in memory, causing high RAM usage and CPU tracking overhead.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** AsNoTracking() speeds up read queries by 20-30% and reduces memory footprint, but disables identity resolution and automatic change tracking for updates.

qa.q: What is Metric Math in Grafana's CloudWatch integration and give a concrete pipeline example?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Metric Math lets you define a query that's a mathematical expression over other queries in the same panel, referenced by their letter (A, B, C...). For an error-rate panel: query A pulls ValidationErrors (Sum), query B pulls RecordsProcessed (Sum), and query C is the expression 100*(A/B), which Grafana evaluates server-side via CloudWatch and renders as a single error-rate-percentage time series -- no client-side math needed.

qa.q: How does a CloudWatch-dimension-driven template variable avoid building 50 separate dashboards?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** A template variable of type Query, pointed at the CloudWatch data source's dimension_values() function, populates a dropdown (e.g. $source) from the actual Source dimension values present in your metrics -- Bloomberg, ICE, Refinitiv, etc. Every panel in the dashboard references $source instead of a hardcoded value, so switching the dropdown re-filters all panels simultaneously. Adding a 51st source requires zero dashboard changes -- it just appears in the dropdown once it starts publishing metrics.
